abstract: Most genome-wide association studies (GWASs) and polygenic score (PGS) models for lung function are based on European-ancestry individuals. Here, we performed GWASs in 17,738 Chinese individuals from the Dongfeng-Tongji (DFTJ) and Wuhan-Zhuhai (WHZH) cohorts, followed by meta-analysis with lung function GWASs from the China Kadoorie Biobank (sample size, n = 100,285), the Taiwan Biobank (n = 62,901), and European-ancestry studies (n = 400,102). Multi-ancestry fine-mapping pinpoints four novel candidate causal variants: one insertion (rs56381615, LINC02270) and three SNPs (rs6941411, PTK7; rs13315867, EPHA3; and rs2713769, ABI3BP). Cross-ancestry genetic correlations are high (0.682-0.811) but significantly lower than 1 (p < 0.005). Transcriptome-wide association analysis across 16 tissues identifies 1,374 genes, including PTK7, CUL7, and EPHA3 as leading novel candidates. Finally, we develop multi-ancestry PGS models that outperform existing models. Overall, this study quantifies cross-ancestry genetic correlation, prioritizes candidate genes, and enhances PGS prediction accuracy of lung function traits in East Asian populations.
